# AI Film Master Guide

The master guide to professional AI filmmaking: Higgsfield mastery, pro craft,
animated and photorealistic tracks, competition-entry craft. Static site + API.
Private research repo. Full text: `llms-full.txt`.

## Guide (human-readable site)

Generated static site in `site/` — rebuild with `python3 scripts/build_site.py`
after editing chapters. Open `site/index.html`.

- `site/index.html` — landing: track picker (animated vs photorealistic), chapter grid, learning paths (7: first film, competition, animated, photoreal, long-form, first 60-second short, the 90-day filmmaker)
- `site/<section>/<chapter>.html` — 30 chapters with sidebar nav, table of contents, prev/next; every chapter shows its honest read time (200 wpm from actual word count) and prints cleanly via `@media print` (`assets/css/print.css`)
- `site/teardown.html` — shot-by-shot teardown viewer: Passport Rush, ONEIRIC, the Grok Odyssey $100K winner, Google DeepMind's Dear Upstairs Neighbors, Fountain 0's Dreams of Violets (75-min Tribeca 2026 AI feature, $2K budget), Nikolay Shestak's The First Honest Day ($450K Astana 2026 Grand Prix winner; tools undisclosed — the teardown is honest about the gap), StoReel's The $150 Microdrama ('Off Campus' experiment: four AI episodes in four days, documented clip by clip), and Robert Gaudette's 'A Face Only a Mother Could Love' (8-minute solo short: $50K Runway AIFF 2026 Grand Prix + Reply AI Film Festival 2026 winner; character sheets before shot one, lip-sync in the prompt, redub for the voice; tool identity reported, not audited), and Tim Simmons' Dragon Blue (hyper-stylized AI action short, solo in two days with Claude Cowork as the production office: reference grids before video, filter-safety memory, token discipline; self-reported, skill published), and Svedka's 'Shake Your Bots Off' (first primarily AI-generated Super Bowl commercial, Super Bowl LX: Silverside AI rebuilt the lost Fembot mascot on component-based ComfyUI workflows — characters, world, choreography as separate controls; crowdsourced TikTok dance integrated in hours; vendor-hosted case study, corroborated by ADWEEK/TechCrunch) broken into shots (setup / what works / what breaks / craft lesson, labeled prompt reconstructions where the stack is documented); data in `data/v1/teardowns.json`
- `site/manifesto.html` — positioning: a living free reference, not a course; everything sourced; what it won't do
- `site/field-guides/` — printable one-pagers generated from the guide's own data: model quick-reference (from `models.json`), prompt anatomy cheat sheet, consistency & dead-eyes checklist
- `site/api.html` — human-readable API docs + a Try-the-API console (endpoint picker, fetch, pretty-printed JSON), and pointers to `AGENT.md`
- `site/skills.html` — browsable skills library with live filter
- `site/budget.html` — interactive credit-budget calculator
- `site/optimizer.html` — budget optimizer: runtime + dialogue share + quality bar → optimal model mix per bucket from `models.json`, with 5×/20× cost envelopes
- `site/shots.html` — shot-list builder: per-shot type/model/seconds/takes → live cost table from `models.json`, totals with 5×/20× envelopes, localStorage lists, JSON export/import, one-click handoff to the optimizer
- `site/doctor.html` — failure doctor: pick the symptom (face morph, dead eyes, plasticky skin…) → craft diagnosis + fix + deep link into the workshop's repair templates; 12 diagnoses in `data/v1/diagnoses.json` (+ schema)
- `site/linter.html` — prompt linter: paste any prompt → structural analysis against the ten-layer anatomy (layers present/missing, vague words flagged, concrete fix per gap); heuristic, honest about it; one-click handoffs to the workshop and anatomy builder (`assets/js/linter.js`)
- `site/cutting-room.html` — the cutting room, playable: type a weak prompt, roll the camera — a shot-by-shot shoot built from the real 47-template prompt library (`data/v1/prompt-templates.json`), real ten-layer analysis, guided fix-bay techniques quoted from real templates (cited by id), real cost math from the Watchtower pricing API with static fallback; take-by-take improvement loop (`assets/js/cutting-room.js`)
- `site/models/` — model deep dives: one page per model (32) + index, generated from `data/v1/models.json` at build time — spec record, worked cost math (USD at $0.0392/credit), use-when/avoid-when from the model's own fields, prompt tips linking the guide's chapters
- `site/anatomy.html` — anatomy of a prompt: interactive nine-layer annotated example + build-your-own mode
- `site/workshop.html` — interactive prompt workshop (template × model × track, save/rate, optional style-bible prepend from `site/style-bible.html`)
- `site/style-bible.html` — style-bible builder: describe character/world once → reusable STYLE LOCK block; named bibles in localStorage (`afg-style-bibles`), copy/save/export/import, workshop integration
- `site/episode-planner.html` — episode planner: lock a mini-drama series (title, logline, hashtag, cast with voice IDs + anchors), plan episode blocks (one emotion, 3–5 beats, turn, cliffhanger), arc tracker with lessons; saved blocks feed one-click 'Send series to Studio' — the planner stages title/logline/cast anchors/every block's format, runtime, and beats into the Studio's series mode; localStorage (`afg-episode-series`)
- `site/hook-generator.html` — hook-title generator: `[Episode N] + [one-line emotional stake] + [CTA]` → 5 worked caption variants, each with a why-this-hooks note
- `site/studio.html` — Studio 2.0 — AI-film studio simulator: a standalone film (title, logline, genre/mood, runtime, draft/festival tier) or a serialized series (3–10 episodes, one of the 5 proven serialized format presets: mini-drama / POV micro-series / day-in-the-life / revenge arc / interactive — each pre-filling runtime band, beat structure, hook style, the dialogue-budget rule) in → deterministic production packet — shot list with per-shot prompts built from the 47-template library, per-shot model picks from `models.json` with cost math, budget table with 5×/20× envelopes, shooting schedule, series bible with locked prompt DNA + locked-anchor asset reuse, self-contained HTML/Markdown packet export (download, print), localStorage plans with names, duplicate, delete, continue-planning; one-click 'Send to Studio' bridge from the episode planner
- `site/greenlight.html` — the green light — a studio meeting, playable: pitch a film concept (title, logline, genre, runtime, resolution, draft/festival ambition) → a six-layer cold read (someone to watch, something happening, a camera decision, light, place and time, a feeling) with a 0–100 score → the shot list from the real 47-template prompt library via the Studio engine → every shot priced from `data/v1/pricing.json` (per-second tiers, low/high ranges, tier + arithmetic shown per shot) → day-by-day schedule → verdict: GREEN LIGHT / CONDITIONAL / BACK TO THE ROOM. The money rule: festival ambition only unlocks flagship pricing when the read clears 55/100 — a cold read gets draft money, stated on the record. Punch-up buttons add craft layer by layer and re-run the plan (watch the money move). Hype hygiene: Veo 4 doesn't exist (SEO bait — verified Oct 2026), Kling 4.0 is announced-not-shipped, Sora discontinued — named and corrected, never priced. Markdown export, print. Takes from the cutting room walk straight in (`assets/js/greenlight.js`, engine unit-tested in `scripts/greenlight.test.js`)
- `site/quiz.html` — model-picker quiz: 5 questions → ranked top-3 from `models.json` with cost math, one-click handoff to the workshop
- `site/compare.html` — model compare: 2–3 models side by side (cost, best use, strengths, weaknesses, native audio, status/last-verified) from `models.json`, shareable via URL params; discontinued excluded
- `site/gallery.html` — prompt gallery: your workshop-saved prompts (localStorage) browsable, filterable by track/model, sortable by rating, open-in-workshop deep links, JSON export/import
- `site/model-watch.html` — the Watchtower 2.0 — model status with a memory: all 32 models with last-verified dates, status, what changed, sources; a since-your-last-visit panel (the browser remembers your last visit in localStorage; live from `/api/models-changes`, recomputed locally from the static files when the function is down), a drift board (flagged checks, failed checks, unwatched models, unpublished rates — severity per model from the drift engine in `server/lib/drift.js`, mirrored in `assets/js/watchtower-lib.js`), pricing changes diffed mechanically against the 2026-10-11 baseline in `data/v1/model-history.json`, and the full dated event log; "verify live before spending" banner; generated from `models.json` + `model-checks.json` + `pricing.json` + `model-history.json` at build time
- `site/checks/` — knowledge checks: 6 scenario-based quizzes (5 questions each) for prompt engineering, directing performance, character consistency, long-form pipelines, sound/music/audio, rights & disclosure; answers explain why, progress in localStorage (`assets/js/checks.js`, data in `scripts/checks.json`)
- `site/changelog.html` — dated changelog rebuilt from git history
- `site/skill-spec.html` — the skill frontmatter+sections format as a spec
- `site/search-index.json` — client-side search index (Ctrl+K palette)

Interactive in-context glossary: `assets/js/glossary.js` wraps the 79 `glossary.json` terms in chapter prose (first occurrence per page) with hover/focus/tap popover definitions.

Chapters (source Markdown, also the canonical text):
- `higgsfield/` — platform-mastery, prompt-engineering, soul-id-deep-dive, competition-entry-craft
- `field/` — 2026-developments (Tribeca's Dreams of Violets, 2026 model field, Sora shutdown, long-form workflow consensus, India/Pakistan AI cinema)
- `craft/` — story-structure, cinematic-language, character-consistency, directing-performance, color-grading, sound-music-audio, editing-pipeline, editing-ai-footage, longform-pipelines, agentic-production-office, component-based-generation, episodic-shortform, documentary-ethics, failure-gallery, ai-film-business
- `distribution/` — release-paths, festival-landscape-2026 (Astana's $450K Grand Prix economics, Reply/Runway/Tirana/MEGA, what wins and why)
- `legal/` — rights-and-disclosure
- `platforms/` — field-guide, when-to-use-what
- `economics/` — credit-math
- `case-studies/` — competition-teardowns, entry-craft-teardowns
- `sources/` — source-index
- `guides/` — first-short (7-day plan: zero to one finished 60-second short)

Note: competitions are covered only as craft teachers (constraints, judging
criteria, delivery discipline). No prizes, deadlines, or promotional material.

## API (static JSON, versioned)

Base: `data/v1/` — rebuild with `python3 scripts/build_api.py` (reads the
research artifacts; outputs committed).

- `data/v1/index.json` — manifest: every endpoint with description, schema URL, `updated` timestamp, record counts, deprecation notes; `meta.version` 1.1.0; repo-level agent guide at `AGENT.md`
- `data/v1/models.json` — 32 models: platform, type, credit costs, strengths, weaknesses, best use, plus per-model `last_verified`, `status` (active/reported/announced/discontinued), `what_changed`, `sources`; explicit `unverified` list. Refreshed 2026-10-11: Sora discontinued, Kling 4.0 announced, MiniMax H3 / Midjourney V1 Video / Seedance 3.0 (reported) added. See `data/v1/model-updates.md`
- `data/v1/prompt-templates.json` — 47 templates: 15 core (`t1`–`t15`), 8 animated (`a1`–`a8`), 8 photorealistic (`p1`–`p8`), 5 performance (`f1`–`f5`), 4 audio (`s1`–`s4`), 4 longform (`l1`–`l4`), 3 repair (`r1`–`r3`); anatomy, use, models
- `data/v1/camera-movements.json` — 22-move camera lexicon with prompt phrasing and use cases
- `data/v1/checklists.json` — pre-production, per-shot, continuity, audio, delivery checklists
- `data/v1/glossary.json` — 79 AI film / production terms
- `data/v1/competitions.json` — judged competitions as craft records: what they judge, production constraints, craft lessons; no prizes or deadlines
- `data/v1/teardowns.json` — shot-by-shot teardowns (Passport Rush, ONEIRIC, Grok Odyssey $100K winner, Dear Upstairs Neighbors, Dreams of Violets, The First Honest Day, The $150 Microdrama, Gaudette's 'A Face Only a Mother Could Love', Simmons' Dragon Blue — The Production Office, Svedka's 'Shake Your Bots Off' — The Lost Fembot): setup, what works, what breaks, craft lesson per shot; prompt reconstructions labeled as analytical, not actual prompts
- `data/v1/diagnoses.json` — failure-diagnosis map for the Doctor tool: 12 symptoms → craft diagnosis, fixes, repair-template link, source chapters
- `data/v1/model-checks.json` — model-watch freshness feed: per-model last check, source-signature diffs, news headlines
- `data/v1/model-review-queue.json` — pending model-watch review items (empty = nothing pending)
- `data/v1/model-history.json` — Watchtower 2.0 event log: dated status/price/tier/release/verification/coverage events per model + the 2026-10-11 pricing baseline the drift engine diffs the live pricing table against
- `data/v1/model-review-log.json` — Watchtower review log: the adjudication record for checker flags — every flag re-fetched and given a verdict with its basis before the queue clears (Watchtower 2.2)
- `data/v1/schema/` — JSON Schema (draft-07) for EVERY endpoint: index, model, prompt-template, camera-movement, checklist, glossary, competition, teardown, diagnosis, model-checks, model-review-queue, model-history, model-review-log
- `AGENT.md` — how an agent uses this repo: base URL pattern, example requests, five end-to-end workflows (Studio planning, prompt linting, model price tracking, mini-drama series setup, microdrama run economics) — executable via `node scripts/agent-workflows.test.js`

## Skills (agentic task procedures)

234 skills in `skills/` — rebuild with `python3 scripts/build_skills.py`
(generates from `data/v1/` data + authored procedures; outputs committed).
`skills/index.json` is the manifest: id, title, description, path per skill.

For agents: load the skill whose task matches the request — skills are the
primary interface for *doing* work; the JSON endpoints are the data layer.
`data/v1/index.json` points here (`repository`, `skills`, `for_agents`).

Categories: prompts (47), camera (22), models (31), checklists (5),
longform (12), techniques (7), craft (20), entry (4), workflow (13),
episodes (5), compare (10), fix (6), budget (3), delivery (3), audio
(5), recipes (12), styles (8), performance (9), grading (3),
distribution (2), legal (4).

## Key facts agents should know

- Higgsfield pricing (read live 2026-10-10): Starter $19/mo annual = 270 credits;
  Plus $47/mo annual = 1,200; Ultra $99/mo annual = 3,000. Verify live before budgeting.
- Credit costs in `models.json` are Higgsfield credits per 5s unless noted.
- Long-form rule: 5–20× generation overhead; assets before shots; registry as production database.

## Known limitations

- Some per-model costs unverified (Seedance 2.5, Soul Cinema, Luma/Pika on
  Higgsfield) — listed in `models.json` → `unverified`.
